timeOrigin: entry interface (top of the Martian atmosphere) = 0 s
caveat: Only numbers stated on the cited NASA pages are used. Times that NASA states relative to another event are added up and marked 'derived'. NASA publishes altitude triggers (not clock times) for terrain-relative navigation and the sky crane, so those phases carry the nearest sourced time bound and say so in the note. Planned values from the 2020 press kits (EDL varies by about a minute). Phases with "trigger": "altitude" are shown by altitude (altitudeKmStart to altitudeKmEnd), not by clock time.

phases.label: Cruise stage separation
phases.note: About 10 minutes before entry the cruise stage is shed. Time derived from 'about 10 minutes before entry'.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

phases.label: Entry interface and guided entry
phases.note: Reaches the top of the Martian atmosphere at about 19,500 kph (12,100 mph). Small thrusters on the aeroshell adjust lift for guided entry. Ends at peak heating.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

phases.label: Peak heating
phases.note: Peak heating about 75 s after entry; heat shield surface reaches about 1,300 C (2,370 F). The vehicle then decelerates until the parachute deploys.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

phases.label: Parachute deploy (Range Trigger)
phases.note: About 240 s after entry at about 11 km altitude and about 1,512 kph (940 mph). 21.5 m (70.5 ft) parachute. End time derived: heat shield separates 20 s after deployment.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

phases.label: Heat shield separation
phases.note: 20 s after parachute deployment (derived: 240 + 20). Reveals the radar and the cameras. Radar is active from here to touchdown, about 7 to 8 km (4 to 5 miles) above the surface.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

phases.label: Radar acquires the ground
phases.note: After heat shield separation the landing radar is exposed and starts measuring altitude and velocity, about 7 to 8 km (4 to 5 miles) above the surface, and runs until touchdown. Time bounds: heat shield separation (260 s, derived) to back shell separation (350 s, derived).

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

phases.label: Terrain-Relative Navigation
phases.note: Lander Vision System compares camera images with an onboard map at about 4.2 to 2.2 km above the ground, locating the vehicle to about 40 m in under 10 s and able to shift touchdown by up to 600 m (2,000 ft). NASA gives altitudes, not clock times, for this step: it is shown only while the altitude is between 4.2 and 2.2 km; the time bounds are heat shield separation (260 s) and back shell separation (350 s, derived).

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

phases.label: Back shell and parachute separation
phases.note: About 90 s after heat shield separation (derived: 260 + 90), powered descent vehicle about 2.1 km (1.3 miles) above the surface.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Launch Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing (90 s) and Landing Press Kit (2.1 km)

phases.label: Powered descent
phases.note: Begins at about 306 kph (190 mph) and 2.1 km (6,900 ft); slows to about 2.7 kph (1.7 mph) at about 20 m (66 ft). End bound is touchdown at about 420 s ('EDL ends about seven minutes later'); NASA gives the end as an altitude.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

phases.label: Sky crane
phases.note: Starts when the descent stage is 20 m (65 ft) over the target; cords lower the rover 7.6 m (25 ft) below the descent stage. NASA gives an altitude trigger, not a clock time: the phase is shown whenever the descent stage is 20 m or less above the ground before touchdown (about 420 s), and its timeline mark sits at the touchdown bound.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

phases.label: Touchdown
phases.note: EDL ends about seven minutes after entry with the rover stationary on the surface; connecting cords are then cut and the descent stage flies away.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing
